title: GIVE GOD THE BEST OF THE BEST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Your offering will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress. In this way you also will present an offering to the Lord from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. From these tithes you must give the Lord's portion to Aaron the priest. You must present as the Lord's portion the best and holiest part of everything given to you.'" — Num 18:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats a theme we have seen before, but now directed at the Levites: "You must present... the best and holiest part of everything given to you." Even the Levites' offering back to God was to be the finest portion, not the scraps. God consistently calls for the best, from priests and Levites and people alike.

Why does God care about the quality of what we give? Not because He needs anything, but because what we give reveals what we truly think of Him. To offer God our best declares that He is worthy of our best. To offer Him our leftovers whispers that He ranks below our own comforts and priorities. Our giving is a mirror of our hearts.

This searches us gently. When we give to God — our time, our energy, our resources — do we give Him the prime of our day or the exhausted remnants? The first fruits of our income or what happens to be left over? God is not impressed by quantity, but He does look at whether we honour Him as worthy of our best.

And we give our best not to earn anything, but in response to the One who gave His best for us. God did not offer us the leftovers of His love; He gave the best and holiest gift of all, His own Son. The Father held nothing back. In light of such extravagant grace, offering God our best becomes not a burden but a delight — the natural response of a heart amazed by how much it has received.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give God the prime of your day and resources, or the leftovers?
2. What does the quality of your giving reveal about your view of God?
3. How does God giving His best in Christ transform your giving into delight?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are worthy of my very best, and You gave Your best in Christ, holding nothing back. Forgive me when I offer You leftovers. Make my giving a joyful response to Your extravagant grace. Amen.
